content:
It's not just a simple call for papers.
It's a struggle against the system.
This time, the pen is your weapon again !

We are trying to put together an edited volume of short essays called "Bigdi Hui Ladki" — looking at how North Indian society keeps adult women perpetually treated as dependents, through patriarchy, financial control, and social hierarchy. We’re hoping to keep it cross-disciplinary — sociology, philosophy, literature, economics, political science, humanities broadly — so please bring whatever lens feels right to you.

We’d really value your voice in this, if you’re open to contributing a piece (roughly 2,000–3,500 words, English/Hindi/mixed, whatever suits your argument). 

We’ve loosely organised it around four themes — Śāsana (control), Āśraya (dependence), Darjā (hierarchy), and Vidroha (refusal) — but there’s plenty of room for your own angle, and I'd love to have your thoughts on the framing itself.

Just let me know if this is something you’d consider, and if any particular theme comes to mind. Happy to share more details once you’re in.

Really, really looking forward to your replies and contributions💙
